name: Rusta AB
reason: Swedish discount home/leisure retailer with diluted EPS SEK 1.72 to 3.59 (2022-25) and consensus +21%/+18%/+11%, but the public record is only 4 years (IPO 2023), untested in a weak consumer market, EBIT margin is at its 100th-pctile high (7.1% vs 6.2% avg) and 10y avg ROIC is just 7.6%.

name: Rentokil Initial plc
reason: Route-density pest-control franchise with GBP adjusted EPS 0.12 to 0.30 (2015-23), but the levered Terminix deal (acq/FCF 0.87, shares +3.3%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 2.58x) has stalled EPS at 0.26 (5y CAGR 3.8%) with a 55% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and unresolved North America integration.

name: Grafton Group PLC
reason: Builders' merchant tied to the Irish/UK/European construction cycle: adjusted EPS fell 0.97 to 0.70 (2022-24, GBP), revenue CAGR only 1.3%, 10y avg ROIC 7.5% and EBIT margin swung 5.3-12.2%; cheap but ordinary with no moat.

name: Deutsche Wohnen SE
reason: Vonovia-controlled Berlin residential landlord with FFO/share EUR 1.63 (2020) down to 1.19 (2025), net debt/EBITDA 12.5x, 10y avg ROIC 4.1% and rents capped by German regulation; rate- and policy-driven, no growth route to 7%.

name: Rubis SCA
reason: Fuel/LPG/bitumen distributor in Africa and the Caribbean whose adjusted EPS rose only EUR 1.96 to 2.98 in 10y (4.3% CAGR, -43% in 2020), with consensus FY2-FY3 +6%/+2%, energy-transition volume risk and EM FX translation exposure.

name: Eurocommercial Properties NV
reason: Shopping-centre landlord with FFO/share EUR 2.01 (2016) to 2.42 (2025), about 2%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 8.2x and consensus +4-6%; forecastable but far below 7% growth and rate-sensitive.

name: Boliden AB
reason: Zinc/copper miner and smelter whose EPS is set by metal prices (SEK 43.96 in 2022 to 22.21 in 2023, -49.5%; EBIT margin 8.5-18.3%); commodity earner fails the forecastability test.

name: Recordati S.p.A.
reason: Specialty/rare-disease pharma with steady adjusted EPS EUR 0.95 to 3.08 (12.4% 10y CAGR, 8/10 years >=7%), but growth relies on acquired/in-licensed products (Isturisa, EUSA; acq/FCF 0.49, net debt 2.2x), a 32% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and patent/competition risk on key rare-disease drugs within 5-10 years.

name: RTL Group S.A.
reason: Linear TV broadcaster in structural decline: adjusted EPS EUR 4.49 (2015) to 0.13 (2025), EBIT margin 17.7% to 6.1% (9th pctile) and flat revenue for 10y as audiences and ad budgets shift to streaming platforms.

name: adidas AG
reason: Strong global brand recovering under new management (adjusted EPS EUR 1.25 in 2022 to 7.46 in 2025, consensus +23%/+26%), but EPS has collapsed twice in 6 years (-78% 2020, -83% 2022), 2025 EPS is still below 2019's 9.70, brand heat and Nike competition are cyclical, and tariff/USD translation risk is high.

name: Alkermes Public Limited Company
reason: Neuroscience biopharma only recently profitable (EBIT margin -35.7% in 2015 to 17.2% in 2025, 10y avg ROIC 0.3%), with USD adjusted EPS swinging 2.89 to 1.43 and consensus FY1 -138% after the Avadel deal; earnings hinge on Vivitrol/Aristada/Lybalvi patents and pipeline outcomes.

name: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE
reason: Dominant luxury house portfolio (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Hennessy) under Arnault with adjusted EPS EUR 7.19 to 22.29 (12.0% 10y CAGR, 7/10 years >=7%), 15% avg ROIC, net debt 0.94x EBITDA and margin at the 64th pctile; EPS is 0.73x its 2023 peak after a luxury downturn and consensus FY2-FY3 is +8.6%/+9.1%, though USD/Asia translation risk applies.

name: Kalmar Corporation
reason: Port and heavy-logistics equipment maker spun out of Cargotec in 2024 with only 3 years of standalone EPS (EUR 3.03 to 1.99 to 2.54), EBIT margin at its 100th-pctile high (12.6% vs 9.6% avg) and earnings tied to the trade/port capex cycle.

name: CVC Capital Partners plc
reason: Private-markets manager whose EPS depends on fundraising, deployment and performance fees/carry (EUR EPS 1.19 in 2021 to 0.21 in 2024 to 0.77 in 2025), with a 135% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; capital-markets earnings are unforecastable, consistent with BX/ARES in the US run.

name: Podravka d.d.
reason: Croatian branded food and pharma group with consensus EPS growth of only -4.5%/+3.4%/+4.7%, recent growth driven by acquisitions (acq/FCF 1.19, net debt 2.82x), 10y avg ROIC 8.2% and a sparse adjusted-EPS record; cheap but ordinary with state-linked ownership.

name: Bureau Veritas SA
reason: Durable testing/inspection/certification oligopolist with 10y avg ROE 27.8% and FCF conversion 1.48, but adjusted EPS grew only EUR 0.96 to 1.42 over 10y (4.0% CAGR, 5.7%/yr from 2019) with EBIT margin at its 100th-pctile high (14.6%); a >=7% route depends on consensus +7-8% being met for the first time.

name: Bellway p.l.c.
reason: UK housebuilder whose earnings follow the housing and mortgage-rate cycle: adjusted EPS GBP 4.36 (2019) to 1.34 (2024) and 1.86 (2026), EBIT margin 22% to 10%; consistent with US homebuilder NOs.

name: Evonik Industries AG
reason: Diversified German chemicals producer with adjusted EPS EUR 2.41 (2015) to 1.36 (2025) (-5.6% 10y CAGR), EBIT margin 13.8% to 6.1%, 10y avg ROIC 4.3% and exposure to commodity feedstock and European energy costs; fails on growth and economics.

name: Petrol dd Ljubljana
reason: State-influenced Slovenian fuel retailer/energy trader with an EBIT margin of -0.6% to 4.0%, fuel prices subject to government caps (2022 loss year) and an adjusted-EPS record that stops in 2020; earnings are set by policy and commodity margins.

name: Zehnder Group AG
reason: Radiator and heat-recovery ventilation maker with a secular energy-efficiency angle and net cash, but adjusted EPS CHF 5.25 (2021) to 3.08 (2024) follows the European construction cycle, GAAP EBIT margin fell to 7.9% (18th pctile) and the 385% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap makes the earnings base unclear.
